experiments.question: Can Deribit DVOL implied volatility be used as a NOCTUA feature, given its coverage?
experiments.rule: Structural measurement, not a hypothesis test. Pre-registered check: count episodes with a strictly-causal IV observation at anchor-1h, separately for train / calib / test. If train coverage is far below test coverage, a plain feature-column design is INADMISSIBLE, because the missingness indicator would be informative in training and constant at test.
experiments.result: Re-derived directly from model/artifacts/episodes.parquet and data/newdata/dvol_btc.parquet. DVOL: 47,563 hourly rows, 2021-03-24 -> 2026-08-26, no duplicate timestamps, uniform 3600s spacing. Episodes: 510,496 over 127,915 unique anchors, 2012-01-01 -> 2026-08-09. Causal join at anchor-3600s: 188,583 episodes covered (36.94%). BY SPLIT: train (<= 2023-06-30) 79,488 of 401,401 = 19.8%; calib 17,756 of 17,756 = 100%; test (>= 2024-01-01) 91,339 of 91,339 = 100%. The asymmetry is total: IV is absent from 80% of training and present for every calibration and test episode. This is a hard design constraint, not a data-quality problem -- DVOL simply did not exist before 2021-03.
experiments.implication: A naive `iv_level` column with a fill value would let the trainer learn from the fill-vs-real distinction, which has zero variance at test time. Two admissible designs remain: (a) refit the whole model on the covered era only, paying ~80% of the training data for the feature; or (b) leave NOCTUA untouched and fit an IV-conditioned RESIDUAL correction on the covered training slice (2021-03 -> 2023-06, 79,488 episodes), calibrate on the fully-covered calib split, score on the fully-covered test split. (b) is strictly safer: it cannot degrade the base model, and its failure mode is a correction of zero.

experiments.question: Can Deribit DVOL implied volatility be used as a NOCTUA feature, given its coverage?

The repository's actual boundaries are noctua.splits.SAMPLE_START = 2017-08-01, TRAIN_END = 2023-01-01, CALIB_END = 2024-07-01, with a per-boundary embargo of H_max hours -- and SAMPLE_START alone drops 2012-2017, which iv-coverage silently counted as training data. Superseded numbers, do not quote: 19.8% / 100% / 100% on n = 401,401 / 17,756 / 91,339. DVOL itself is unchanged and was re-verified: 47,563 rows, 2021-03-24 -> 2026-08-26, every gap exactly 3600s, 0 duplicates.

experiments.lesson: Split boundaries are data, not folklore. I typed plausible dates rather than reading noctua/splits.py, and a sonnet agent that read the file got it right. The error was invisible in the qualitative story -- both versions say 'train coverage is far below test' -- which is exactly the kind of wrong number that stays in circulation.

GUARDS: calm QLIKE not worse by more than 1%; deep-tail MCB not worse with a CI excluding zero unfavourably; pooled QLIKE reported but NOT a condition; log_har_gauss re-scored rather than held fixed. experiments.implication: The CI excludes zero UNFAVOURABLY, which the pre-registered rejection clause did not name -- it was written for 'contains zero'. This is a SIGN REVERSAL against 12's Arm 4 (-10.44% spike on an OLS-only harness), not a wash-out. Mechanism: the full pipeline already feeds har_1h/har_6h to the neural stage, so the treatment adds no information and instead moves the noisiest available RV window into the term whose job is stability. 19's framing is corrected: the anchor's blindness below a day is what the anchor is FOR, not a defect. Redirects to the blend weight, which 19 itself named as the next test.
experiments.lesson: A rule that has to be reinterpreted after the fact is doing less work than it appears to. The rejection clause covered 'no effect' but not 'effect in the opposite direction', and the second is a different scientific claim.

experiments.question: Did E-anchor's pre-registered condition actually consult the data?

The rule asked `primary = sp_hi < 0.0`, and `nan < 0.0` is False, so the script printed 'DO NOT ADOPT' without any statistic having looked at the data. The verdict was right by luck: all six folds moved the wrong way. Re-derived through --from-json, the spike CI is [+0.02151, +0.05408] and the verdict is unchanged.
experiments.implication: Added direction.mean_ci (defined at every usable n; returns the pre-registered moving-block interval AND the iid interval AND the sign count, so the estimator choice at n = 6 is visible rather than picked), direction.ci_excludes_zero (raises on a NaN interval), and research/pitfalls.check_ci_is_defined as check 11 with this run as its historical case -- the self-test now expects 11 failures. anchor_freshness.py gained --from-json so a broken STATISTIC can be corrected through the same code path without retraining and without any opportunity to change a SCORE.
experiments.lesson: NaN silently satisfies every 'did not clear the bar' branch, so the rule returns the same answer whether the effect is huge, zero, or unmeasured. A correct answer is not evidence that the machinery works.

experiments.question: Is a state-dependent ensemble weight (spike vs calm) better than the shipped constant 0.25?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered in eval/blend_ceiling.py and committed before the run. PRIMARY: pooled QLIKE of the walk-forward two-state SHRUNK rule vs w = 0.25, CI excluding zero favourably. Shrinkage w = 0.25 + lam*(mean_f argmin - 0.25), lam = m/(m + (sd/0.25)^2), all constants a priori (Blanc & Setzer, Management Science 2020). The RAW argmin is reported beside it as the estimator the combination-puzzle literature predicts will lose. GUARDS: spike QLIKE not worse; calm not worse by >1%; RAW weights must not straddle 0.25 in both directions. Pre-condition: the TWO-STATE in-sample oracle ceiling must clear 2% (amended from a per-episode oracle before any fold ran, because that fits one parameter per observation and would clear any floor).
experiments.result: 6 folds x 3 seeds, 5 scored. SHRUNK pooled +0.00307 CI [-0.01008, +0.02603], better in 4 of 5 folds. RAW pooled +0.01355 CI [-0.00686, +0.05027]. Two-state in-sample oracle ceiling 7.07% (floor cleared); per-episode oracle 31.33% (degenerate, dismissed). Constant-w sweep minimises at w = 0.45, -1.41% vs shipped -- IN-SAMPLE over all six folds, NOT a result. Per-fold oracle weights (calm/spike): 0.65/1.00, 0.35/0.70, 0.00/0.00, 0.70/0.55, 0.45/1.00, 0.80/1.00.
experiments.implication: The headroom is real (7.07%) and unreachable by this state variable. Fold-to-fold sd of the optimal weight is 0.28-0.51 on a [0,1] parameter: 2023 wants w = 0.00 and 2026 wants 0.80. What separates them is not spike-vs-calm but whether volatility is about to collapse. Shrinkage behaved exactly as the literature predicts -- it cut the raw arm's damage 77% without turning a loss into a win.

experiments.question: Is a single walk-forward constant blend weight better than the shipped 0.25?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered in eval/blend_one_state.py and committed BEFORE the run. One estimated parameter instead of two. PRIMARY: pooled QLIKE of the SHRUNK arm vs w = 0.25 at the BONFERRONI-ADJUSTED 97.5% level, because this is the second test on the same forecasts. GUARDS: spike not worse; calm within 1%; and a WORST-FOLD BOUND of 5%, added because infer.BLEND_W's own note records 0.25 was chosen to bound the worst fold at +6.7% against pure NOCTUA's +72.3% in the 2023 collapse. experiments.result: SHRUNK pooled +0.00049, adj CI [-0.01141, +0.01981], better in 4 of 5 folds. RAW +0.01167 adj CI [-0.00872, +0.04383]. Per-fold shrunk deltas: 2022 -0.56%, 2023 +7.84%, 2024 -2.20%, 2025 -3.09%, 2026 -8.59%. PRIMARY fails and the WORST-FOLD guard fails at +7.84% against the 5% bar. pitfalls check_not_a_coin_flip FIRED: n=5, |mean| 0.00049 vs se 0.00876 -- NOT RESOLVABLE at this n.
experiments.implication: Four of five folds improve, several substantially, and the volatility-collapse fold gives it all back -- the exact scenario the guard was pre-registered for. The correct statement about BLEND_W = 0.25 is not 'it is optimal' but '0.25 buys insurance against a 2023 and the premium is about 1.4% of mean QLIKE'. Whether to pay it is a risk-appetite question, not a QLIKE question. Separately: the estimate is 1/18th of its own standard error, so this is a NON-MEASUREMENT, not a null -- it would look identical if the true effect were +2% or -2%. That makes E-power the blocking question.
experiments.lesson: A guard pre-registered from a documented historical failure is worth more than the primary endpoint: the primary was ambiguous and the worst-fold guard was decisive.

experiments.question: Before E-power's numbers exist: how much SHOULD the CI tighten on a 24x wider scoring slice, and what would each outcome mean?
experiments.rule: A prediction recorded BEFORE the result, so the explanation cannot be fitted to it afterwards. Falsifiable: it names a direction and a bound.
experiments.result: PREDICTION: the CI will tighten by MATERIALLY LESS than sqrt(24) = 4.90x. Reason: the fold-level delta variance has two components, and only one of them shrinks. Within-fold sampling error falls as more episodes are scored; between-fold treatment HETEROGENEITY -- 2021 and 2026 are different market regimes and the treatment genuinely does different things in them -- does not fall at all. A wider slice buys the first and nothing of the second. IF the observed tightening is close to 1x, the fold deltas are almost entirely heterogeneity, and no number of extra episodes helps: the binding constraint is the number of YEARS, not the number of episodes, and six folds is six effectively independent observations however many episodes each contains. IF it is close to 4.90x, the fold deltas were nearly pure sampling error and the production slice was simply too small.
experiments.implication: Minimum detectable effect implied by the spread ALREADY on record, at 80% power and alpha = 0.05 two-sided (MDE ~ 2.80 * se): spike QLIKE 0.02685 = 1.44% of its 1.86701 baseline (from E-anchor, n = 6, sd = 0.02349); pooled QLIKE 0.02452 = 8.44% of its 0.29035 baseline (from E-blend-1state, n = 5, sd = 0.01958). These two numbers already reconcile the apparent tension between 21 and 23: the production slice resolved E-anchor's spike effect decisively because that effect was 1.87%, above its 1.44% floor, and could not resolve the blend weight because that effect was 0.17%, far below an 8.4% pooled floor. Neither result was surprising given the resolution; nobody had computed the resolution.
experiments.lesson: If the tightening is small, the follow-up is NOT more episodes -- it is a different ESTIMATOR: a moving-block bootstrap over per-episode paired deltas pooled across folds, rather than a bootstrap over six fold means. The arms are trained separately but scored on identical episode sets, so the deltas are paired and that estimator is available. anchor_freshness currently stores only fold-level summaries, which is the thing to change next.

experiments.question: Does eval/iv_correction.py measure what its pre-registered rule says it measures, BEFORE it is run?
experiments.rule: Audit before the first run, so a defect cannot be discovered after a result exists and then argued about. Every finding re-derived against the code rather than accepted from the agent that reported it.
experiments.result: A sonnet agent audited the file and reported 9 findings; 6 were confirmed against the code and fixed, 3 were style or latent. (1) THE SIGN-STABILITY GUARD WAS DOCUMENTED AND NEVER IMPLEMENTED -- the rule requires RAW coefficient signs not to oscillate across folds and no code tested it; a printed 'signs' column made it look covered, but that column is the sign count of the QLIKE DELTA, a different quantity. Now implemented, restricted to coefficients the shrunk arm leaves materially non-zero. (2) THE CALM GUARD USED THE POOLED BASE AS ITS DENOMINATOR. Re-derived from E-anchor's own numbers: calm 0.19887, pooled 0.29035, so the guard was 1.46x too lenient -- the agent's illustrative example implied 'several times', which is larger than the real figure, and 1.46x is what is recorded. (3) The correction exponent was unclipped in scoring while clipped in fitting. QLIKE is bounded below by 0 and unbounded above, so one extrapolated episode can dominate a fold; the bias is one-directional toward spurious REJECT. Bounded at |z.beta| <= 1 (sigma may scale by at most 2.72x) with exceedances COUNTED and reported. (4) The Newton clip invalidates the gradient where it binds. Now asserted off the boundary. (5) check_arms_matched was passed THE SAME EXPRESSION TWICE -- a check that cannot fail, the mirror of pitfalls check 7's guard that cannot pass. Counts now derived independently. (6) The placebo rotation had no lower-bound guard: on a shorter covered window the modulo wraps to a small near-neighbour shift, decorrelating nothing while still passing the coverage check.
experiments.implication: INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED, not taken on the agent's word: the Newton gradient and Hessian match finite differences to 1.4e-10 and 6.8e-10, the Hessian is PSD, and fit_beta recovers known coefficients and reaches a lower objective than the generating truth. The convexity claim in the docstring holds. One DESIGN decision was made rather than a fix: the spike CI bar stays loose (fail only if the interval lies entirely above zero) because ~20 spike episodes a fold make the strict bar unsatisfiable -- pitfalls check 9's failure mode -- and it is paired with a POINT bar of 2% of the spike baseline so the guard still has teeth.
experiments.lesson: Two of the six defects were guards that could not fail: one documented but absent, one comparing an expression to itself. Both would have printed reassuring output. A guard is not verified by existing -- pitfalls check 7 already says this about guards that cannot pass, and the same argument runs in the other direction.

experiments.question: Does Deribit DVOL implied volatility carry information NOCTUA's own-past-bars cascade does not?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered in eval/iv_correction.py and committed before the run. PRIMARY: pooled QLIKE of the walk-forward SHRUNK correction vs the uncorrected base, on IV-covered test episodes, both arms scored on the SAME episodes, CI excluding zero favourably. GUARDS: must beat a PLACEBO (identical machinery on IV features circularly rotated one year inside the covered era) with a CI excluding zero; spike QLIKE not worse (loose CI bar plus a 2%-of-baseline point bar); calm QLIKE within 1% OF THE CALM BASE; RAW coefficient signs must not oscillate across folds. Cannot ADOPT alone -- barrier curves not rebuilt.
experiments.result: 5 scored folds. Shrunk pooled -0.02320 CI [-0.06199, +0.01381] -- PRIMARY fails. Shrunk SPIKE -1.05579 CI [-1.95499, -0.55027], better in 5 of 5 folds, a 57% improvement -- which on its own would read as a headline result. THE PLACEBO REPRODUCES MORE THAN HALF OF IT: -0.53955, also 5 of 5 folds. The margin between real and placebo is -0.02469 pooled, CI [-0.04184, +0.00395], containing zero. Calm QLIKE WORSENS +0.02869 = +13.52% of the calm base, CI excluding zero. iv_level's raw coefficient flips sign across folds. Three independent guard failures.
experiments.implication: DECOMPOSED: an INTERCEPT-ONLY fit -- a bare scalar multiplying every sigma, no IV features at all -- delivers 72.0% of the spike gain. The fitted scalar is stable across five independently fitted folds: e^a in [1.139, 1.202]. That is not implied volatility, it is the point-forecast functional: infer.py records that QLIKE is minimised by the conditional MEAN of variance while NOCTUA reports the MEDIAN, and that the mean over-forecasts at ratio 1.205. The fit found a value BETWEEN them, ~1.17, and the placebo collects it too because the placebo also has an intercept. This is branch (a) of the failure taxonomy written into ivfeatures.py BEFORE the run: implied vol is persistence in a different costume, its level already carried by har_1d.
experiments.lesson: The placebo arm is now standard for any fitted correction. Without it this reads as a 57% spike improvement, unanimous across folds, with an interval nowhere near zero. It cost one extra fit per fold. Two of the three guard failures came from machinery an audit had fixed hours earlier -- the calm denominator and the sign-stability check that was documented but never implemented -- so with the original code this would have failed only one guard instead of three.

experiments.question: With the intercept removed, do the IV features carry any INCREMENTAL information?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered before the run. Identical to E2 except beta_0 is held at zero in BOTH the real and placebo arms, so the correction can only RESHAPE sigma and never rescale it. Same guards, same shrinkage constants, same population. EXPECTED: near-nothing, since E2's margin over the placebo already contained zero. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE CONCLUSION: if the intercept-free real arm beats the intercept-free placebo with a CI excluding zero, IV carries shape information the intercept was masking and ivfeatures.py's branch (a) is wrong.
experiments.result: pre-registered before the run

experiments.question: Should NOCTUA's point forecast be scaled up from the median toward the QLIKE-optimal mean?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered, QUEUED BEHIND E-power and deliberately not run yet. A lever that trades one slice against another cannot be judged without knowing the resolution, and 22 says that is unmeasured. When it runs: PRIMARY must be stated on BOTH slices (spike and calm), not pooled, because the effect has opposite signs on them and a pooled mean would hide that -- the 13 lesson. Must also re-score the barrier curves, since scaling sigma moves every touch probability, which a median-only re-weighting does not test.
experiments.result: Surfaced as a by-product of E2's decomposition, not sought. A stable scalar e^a in [1.139, 1.202] across five independently fitted folds improves spike QLIKE by ~36% and worsens calm QLIKE by ~13%. infer.py already records the two endpoints -- the median at 1.00 and the mean at 1.205, the latter scoring worse -- so the open question is whether an intermediate point beats both, and at what cost to calibration.

experiments.question: With the intercept removed, do the IV features carry any INCREMENTAL information?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered before the run, identical to E2 except beta_0 held at zero in BOTH arms. The pre-registration also stated in advance what would overturn E2's conclusion: 'if the intercept-free real arm beats the intercept-free placebo with a CI excluding zero, IV carries shape information the intercept was masking and ivfeatures.py branch (a) is wrong.'
experiments.result: THAT IS WHAT HAPPENED, and the rule still rejects on one guard. Shrunk pooled -0.03859 CI [-0.05635, -0.01456] -- PRIMARY PASSES. Placebo margin -0.08381 CI [-0.14822, -0.02069] -- BEATS THE PLACEBO. The placebo now actively HURTS (+0.04522, 0 of 5 folds better), which is what misaligned features with no intercept should do. Spike -0.36898 (-23.15%), calm -0.02172 (-10.24%, an improvement not a degradation). pitfalls: resolvable at n=5, |mean| 0.03859 vs se 0.01174. EVERY GUARD PASSES EXCEPT SIGN STABILITY, which fails on iv_level alone.
experiments.implication: POSITIVE CONTROL, run independently of the placebo: fit exactly as E2b does on history, then SHUFFLE the scored fold's feature rows before applying the correction. Aligned -0.03859 with 4 of 5 folds improved; test-shuffled +0.01530 with 1 of 5. The gain REQUIRES correctly aligned test-fold features, which is what an out-of-sample signal means. So E2's conclusion is PARTLY overturned: branch (a) was right about the LEVEL and wrong about the DYNAMICS. iv_level is the smallest shrunk coefficient (+0.012 in the final fold) and the only one whose sign flips; iv_chg_6h, iv_chg_24h, iv_z_20d and ivrv_ratio are 3-5x larger and stable.
experiments.lesson: E2 and E2b differ by ONE term and reach opposite readings of the same features. A fitted intercept absorbing a known level bias masked a real effect underneath it. Any future correction should be reported with and without its intercept as a matter of course.

experiments.question: Do DVOL's DYNAMICS carry incremental information once its redundant LEVEL is dropped?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered BEFORE the run. Identical to E2b -- no intercept, same shrinkage constants, same placebo, same population -- with iv_level removed from the feature set, leaving iv_chg_1h, iv_chg_6h, iv_chg_24h, iv_z_20d, ivrv_ratio. THIS IS THE THIRD TEST ON THESE FORECASTS, so intervals are at the BONFERRONI-ADJUSTED level for the IV family (alpha = 0.05/3). All E2b guards carry over, sign stability included -- if another coefficient now oscillates, that is a rejection, not an invitation to drop it too. CANNOT ADOPT ALONE: a pass earns a full-pipeline confirmation run that rebuilds the barrier curves, which is a fresh test.
experiments.result: pre-registered before the run. THE SELECTION RISK, STATED PLAINLY: dropping the feature that just failed is a garden-of-forking-paths move. What makes it defensible rather than a post-hoc rescue is that ivfeatures.py's failure taxonomy predicted exactly this split BEFORE any IV experiment ran -- branch (a) said the LEVEL's information would already be carried by har_1d while the premium and the changes might not be. E2b's coefficients match that prediction: iv_level smallest and unstable, the dynamics 3-5x larger and stable. Acting on a written prior prediction is not the same as fishing, but the reader is entitled to weigh it themselves, so both are recorded.

experiments.question: Do DVOL's DYNAMICS carry incremental information once its redundant LEVEL is dropped?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered and committed before the run: E2b minus iv_level, no intercept, same shrinkage constants, same placebo, Bonferroni-adjusted intervals for the third test on these forecasts. All E2b guards carry over, sign stability included. CANNOT ADOPT ALONE.
experiments.result: ALL FIVE CONDITIONS PASS at the 98.33% level. pooled -0.03264 CI [-0.04356, -0.01403], 5 of 5 folds; spike -0.33295 (-20.89%), 5 of 5; calm -0.01744 (-8.22%, an improvement), 4 of 5; placebo margin -0.04533 CI [-0.07323, -0.01420]; RAW signs stable. Spike AND calm both improve, which no previous lever in this project achieved. Coefficients stable across all five independently fitted folds with lam >= 0.85 after the first: iv_chg_1h negative, iv_chg_6h / iv_chg_24h / iv_z_20d / ivrv_ratio positive. A 1-sigma move in iv_chg_24h scales sigma by about 1.06.
experiments.implication: POSITIVE CONTROL: aligned -0.03264 with 5 of 5 folds better; shuffling only the SCORED fold's feature rows gives +0.01909 with 0 of 5. Complete reversal. CAVEAT RECORDED AGAINST THE RESULT: the CI clears zero at alpha/1 through alpha/24, but every interval beyond alpha/3 is IDENTICAL -- five fold-level observations give the bootstrap five distinct values and it cannot widen further. Surviving alpha/24 is an artifact of n, not significance. What carries this is 5-of-5 and the placebo margin. SCOPE: 1,681 episodes, all inside DVOL's era; not claimed before 2021-03.
experiments.lesson: ADVANCE is not ADOPT, and the ledger REFUSED the word the first time it was used because its vocabulary had no such state. That was the ledger working: a state with no name gets folded into a neighbouring one, and folding ADVANCE into ADOPT is how an unconfirmed result reaches an artifact. ADVANCE is now defined in ledger.py.

experiments.question: Does E2c's correction survive the full pipeline, including the barrier curves?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered, QUEUED BEHIND E-power. A FRESH test, not a re-reading of E2c: apply the correction inside the full pipeline and re-score everything the median-only run skipped. PRIMARY: pooled QLIKE on the covered test episodes, CI excluding zero favourably. GUARDS: deep-tail barrier MCB must not worsen with a CI excluding zero unfavourably; Christoffersen conditional coverage at alpha = 5% must not degrade; spike and calm QLIKE must each not worsen; the placebo arm runs again inside the full pipeline. Only a pass here earns a place in the artifact.
experiments.result: pre-registered before the run. Motivation: E2c re-weighted a recorded median and never rebuilt the barrier curves, the committee or the calibration. NOCTUA's product is a touch-probability curve, not a sigma; scaling sigma moves every barrier probability.

experiments.question: Can Deribit DVOL implied volatility be used as a NOCTUA feature, given its coverage?
experiments.rule: Closes the structural measurement. It asked which of two admissible designs to take: (a) refit the model on the covered era only, paying two thirds of the training data, or (b) an IV-conditioned residual correction on cached out-of-sample forecasts.
experiments.result: Design (b) was taken and it worked, subject to confirmation. Coverage is unchanged and still the reason (a) was refused: train 62,051 of 189,831 = 32.7%, calib and test both 100%. E2 REJECTED with an intercept, E2b partly overturned that, E2c ADVANCED on the dynamics alone -- pooled -0.03264 CI [-0.04356, -0.01403], 5 of 5 folds, beating a coverage-preserving placebo. The correction's failure mode was a correction of zero and it was not zero.
experiments.implication: The coverage asymmetry that made a plain feature column inadmissible turned out not to matter for the deployed case: the correction applies only where IV exists, and for SERVING that is every live episode. The 32.7% figure constrains what can be VALIDATED historically, not what can be run. E2-confirm is the remaining gate.

experiments.question: Is the funding rate usable as a forward-looking input, and at what coverage?
experiments.rule: Structural measurement, same protocol as iv-coverage-2: count episodes with a strictly causal observation before the anchor, per split, read through noctua.splits.time_splits rather than assumed. No hypothesis is tested here.
experiments.result: data/newdata/funding_btc.parquet: 64,206 rows, 2019-04-30 10:00 -> 2026-08-26 17:00 UTC, columns timestamp / index_price / interest_8h / interest_1h / prev_index_price / ts / source (deribit). Spacing is hourly at 64,204 of 64,205 gaps; ONE 10,800s gap, i.e. two missing hours in seven years. Causal join at the most recent stamp strictly before the anchor: train 128,635 of 189,831 = 67.8%; calib 52,359 of 52,359 = 100%; test 73,867 of 73,867 = 100%.
experiments.implication: Funding has MORE THAN TWICE DVOL's training coverage -- 67.8% against 32.7% -- because it starts 2019-04-30 rather than 2021-03-24. The residual-correction design that E2c advanced applies unchanged, and at 67.8% the alternative design (a), refitting the model on the covered era, is no longer obviously ruinous the way it was for DVOL. WHY IT IS THE RIGHT NEXT INPUT rather than just the next available one: E2c's result is that a FORWARD-LOOKING input carries volatility information the trailing cascade does not. Funding is the other forward-looking series in this repository -- it prices crowding in perpetual positioning, and crowded positioning is the precondition for a liquidation cascade, which is one mechanism behind the spike episodes carrying 25.8% of total loss. That is a mechanism, not a result.
experiments.lesson: Measure coverage BEFORE designing the experiment. Doing it for DVOL is what ruled out a plain feature column and produced the residual design that eventually worked.

experiments.question: Is E-power's pre-registered primary quantity actually scale-free?
experiments.rule: An amendment recorded BEFORE the run finished and before any CI width was computed, for the same reason the ceiling amendment in blend_ceiling was recorded rather than made silently: a rule changed after seeing the answer is not a rule.
experiments.result: NO, AND THIS IS A DEFECT IN MY OWN PRE-REGISTRATION. BENCHMARK.md 22 made the primary 'block-bootstrap spike-QLIKE CI on the production slice divided by the same CI on the 24-hour slice'. That ratio is ABSOLUTE, and the two slices do not share a scale. From the three folds visible while the run is still going: production-slice spike QLIKE levels are 3.2380 / 1.3542 / 3.6483 against wide-slice 1.1360 / 0.5984 / 1.1163 on the same fold years. A CI on a quantity whose baseline is three times larger is wider for a reason that has nothing to do with precision, so the pre-registered ratio conflates scale with resolution.
experiments.implication: BOTH are reported. The ABSOLUTE ratio because it was pre-registered and changing a rule silently is worse than a flawed rule stated plainly; and the SCALE-NORMALISED ratio -- each CI width divided by that slice's own control spike-QLIKE baseline -- as the interpretable one, since it is the relative resolution that determines what size of effect an experiment can detect. SEPARATELY, and not part of the power question: the relative treatment effect also looks smaller on the wide slice. Production 1.87%; wide slice, first three folds, 0.91% / 1.57% / 1.26%. That is a DIFFERENT finding from a change in precision and must not be reported as one. Two readings will be available and the data here cannot separate them: either the 17:00 anchor genuinely carries a larger treatment effect than other hours, or the production-slice estimate was inflated and the wide slice is regression to the mean. Both will be stated.
experiments.lesson: A ratio of two intervals is only a measure of precision when the two intervals are on the same scale. I wrote the rule while thinking about episode counts and did not check that the quantity being bounded had the same magnitude in both arms.

experiments.question: Is E2c's correction genuinely episode-varying, or a per-fold level shift in disguise?
experiments.rule: A falsification attempt on my own ADVANCE, not a new hypothesis test. Dropping beta_0 forces the correction to average ~0 on the HISTORY folds, not within the scored fold, so a correction with little within-fold spread would still act as a level shift -- the 24 confound in subtler form. Decisive test: replace the varying shift by its own fold mean and see how much of the gain survives.
experiments.result: It is genuinely episode-varying. Within-fold sd of the applied log-shift is 0.0769 / 0.1040 / 0.1043 / 0.0809 / 0.1136 against fold MEANS of +0.0113 / +0.0159 / -0.0024 / -0.0136 / -0.0274 -- a spread 4x to 43x the mean, with the mean changing sign across folds. e^shift spans roughly 0.83 to 1.22 between the 5th and 95th percentiles, so sigma moves about +/-20% at the tails. Replacing the varying shift by its own fold mean captures -0.00342 of the -0.03264 gain: 89.5% OF THE GAIN REQUIRES EPISODE-LEVEL VARIATION.
experiments.implication: This closes the most plausible remaining artifact explanation for E2c. Combined with the placebo margin and the test-shuffle positive control, three independent checks now point the same way. It does NOT change the verdict: still ADVANCE, still not adopted, still awaiting E2-confirm on the barrier curves.
experiments.lesson: Removing an intercept term does not remove the level-shift confound -- it only moves where the constraint binds, from the scored fold to the history folds. The confound has to be measured out, not designed out.

experiments.question: Does E2c's conclusion depend on SIGMA_B, the shrinkage scale fixed a priori at 0.10?
experiments.rule: A robustness check on my own ADVANCE. An a-priori constant is only defensible if the conclusion does not hinge on it, so sweep it including both degenerate endpoints: near-total shrinkage and none at all.
experiments.result: It does not depend on it. Swept 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.50 / 1.00 and unbounded, every value clears zero at the Bonferroni-adjusted 98.33% level. Pooled delta is flat between -0.03180 and -0.03374 across the whole range, softening only under the most aggressive shrinkage (0.01 gives -0.02325, still clearing zero). Fold count is 5 of 5 at SIGMA_B <= 0.05 and 4 of 5 at >= 0.20.
experiments.implication: The flatness is itself a finding: THE SHRINKAGE IS NEARLY INERT HERE, because the coefficients were already stable across folds (lam >= 0.85 after the first). The same estimator was decisive for the blend weight in 23, cutting the raw arm's damage by 77%. The difference is not the estimator but the parameter -- the IV coefficients are stable and the blend weight is not, which is the same contrast the per-fold oracle weights showed with sd 0.28-0.51 on a [0,1] parameter.

experiments.question: What will each possible value of the effective sample-size multiplier mean for the research programme?
experiments.rule: Interpretation bands fixed BEFORE the number exists. The prediction in E-power-prediction named a direction; this names what each outcome CHANGES. Without this, any multiplier can be narrated as confirming whatever was already believed -- and this project has a recorded instance of exactly that in the 9 sigma-atom mechanism, which was explained confidently and backwards.
experiments.result: BANDS, on the SCALE-NORMALISED effective multiplier = (scale-normalised width ratio)^2, against a nominal 24x more episodes. (A) >= 12x, i.e. more than half the nominal gain survives. The production slice was simply too small and the fix is cheap: run future experiments on the 24-hour slice. Re-run E-blend and E-blend-1state there, since both were non-measurements at the narrow resolution. (B) 3x to 12x. A real but partial gain. Widening helps and is worth the ~4x compute, but it does not rescue small effects; each experiment must state a minimum detectable effect in advance and refuse to run below it. (C) 1.5x to 3x. Widening buys little. The binding constraint is the number of YEARS, not episodes, and the remedy is the ESTIMATOR -- the paired per-episode bootstrap -- not more scoring. (D) < 1.5x. Effectively nothing survives. Six folds is six effectively independent observations however many episodes each carries, and the fold-level bootstrap is measuring between-year heterogeneity almost exclusively. Every fold-level verdict in BENCHMARK.md is then a statement about six years, not about thousands of episodes, and the document should say so.
experiments.implication: SEPARATELY AND WITH ITS OWN RULE: if the 21 verdict FLIPS across slices -- spike QLIKE's CI crossing zero or excluding it favourably on the wide slice -- then every prior verdict resting on a marginal interval is re-run before any new experiment starts. That gate is independent of which band the multiplier lands in, and it fires even in band (A). AND A THIRD THING, which is not a power result at all: the relative treatment effect looked smaller on the wide slice in the folds visible mid-run. If that holds, it is a statement about ANCHOR HOURS, not about precision, and this data cannot say whether 17:00 genuinely differs or the production estimate was inflated. It will be reported as unresolved rather than decided.

experiments.question: How much statistical power do this project's verdicts actually have?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered in BENCHMARK.md 22, amended to a scale-free primary before any width was computed, with interpretation bands fixed in E-power-bands before the number existed. All three applied verbatim.
experiments.result: 6 folds x 3 seeds x 2 arms on the 24-anchor-hour slice at H = 19. 341 episodes per fold on the production slice against 8,185 on the wide one, a 24.0x nominal gain. SCALE-NORMALISED spike-QLIKE width ratio 1.24x against sqrt(24) = 4.90x; absolute ratio 3.05x. EFFECTIVE SAMPLE-SIZE MULTIPLIER 1.53x, so 6.4% OF THE NOMINAL GAIN SURVIVES AS USABLE PRECISION. Lands in band (C), 1.5-3x, AT THE BOUNDARY with (D) -- 1.53 against a 1.50 cutoff, which is 'barely (C)' and should be read that way. The prediction recorded before the run -- materially less than 4.90x -- holds.
experiments.implication: NOT PREDICTED AND MORE IMPORTANT THAN THE HEADLINE: the four quantities tighten very unequally. deep-tail MCB 2.98x, calm 2.10x, pooled 1.89x, SPIKE 1.24x. Spike is helped LEAST and spike is where 7a put 25.8% of total loss -- because spike episodes are ~6% of the population, so 24x wider still leaves few of them and what remains is between-year heterogeneity no extra scoring reduces. More data helps most exactly where it is needed least. VERDICT DID NOT FLIP: both slices REJECT with the interval excluding zero unfavourably, so 22's re-run gate does not fire. But the wide slice found harm the narrow one could not resolve -- calm QLIKE REVERSES SIGN from -0.00079 (non-significant) to +0.00102 CI [+0.00062, +0.00249]; the deep-tail MCB guard FAILS where it passed; pooled becomes significant at +0.00170 CI [+0.00125, +0.00343]. 21's rejection is strengthened on three further quantities. EFFECT-SIZE QUESTION, reported unresolved as promised: 1.87% production against 1.65% all-hours. The mid-run impression that the wide-slice effect was much smaller was an artifact of reading three folds; with six the gap is 0.22 points, well inside either interval, and this data cannot say whether 17:00 genuinely differs or the production estimate was inflated.
experiments.lesson: Every fold-level verdict in BENCHMARK.md is a statement about SIX YEARS, not about thousands of episodes. At 6.4% survival the fold-level bootstrap measures year-to-year variation almost exclusively, which makes 23's non-measurement -- an estimate one eighteenth of its own standard error -- the predictable consequence rather than bad luck. Three things change: widening the slice is NOT the fix (24x cost for 1.53x effective n, and worst on the slice that matters); the remedy is the ESTIMATOR, the paired per-episode bootstrap anchor_freshness now records; and a minimum detectable effect becomes a required field, since the production slice's MDEs are ~1.44% on spike and ~8.44% on pooled and an experiment hypothesising less than its slice's MDE is a non-measurement before it runs.

experiments.question: Which scoring slice should E2-confirm run on, now that E-power has measured what each buys?
experiments.rule: A design decision fixed BEFORE the run, because E-power's finding makes it a real choice rather than a default. E-power-result now requires a minimum detectable effect to be stated in advance: an experiment hypothesising less than its slice's MDE is a non-measurement before it runs.
experiments.result: DECISION: run E2-confirm on the PRODUCTION slice, then, only if it passes, re-run on the 24-hour slice as a confirmation of the deep-tail MCB guard specifically. POWER CHECK, as now required. E2c measured pooled -0.03264 against a base near 0.29, about -11.2%. The production slice's pooled MDE is ~8.44%. 11.2% > 8.44%, so the primary endpoint IS adequately powered on the production slice and this is not a non-measurement before it runs.
experiments.implication: WHY PRODUCTION FIRST: E2-confirm is an ADOPTION decision, and the production slice -- H = 19 at 17:00 UTC -- is what ships. E-power also priced the alternative: 24x the compute for 1.53x effective n is a bad trade when the effect is already above the MDE. THE KNOWN WEAKNESS, named in advance rather than discovered later: deep-tail MCB is the quantity that gains MOST from widening (2.98x, the largest of the four E-power measured), and it is a central guard here. So the MCB guard is the least-powered part of this experiment on the production slice. If MCB comes back inconclusive -- CI containing zero rather than clearly favourable -- that is NOT a pass by default; it triggers the wide-slice re-run before anything is adopted.

experiments.question: Does E2c's IV correction survive the full pipeline, including the barrier curves?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered in eval/iv_confirm.py and committed before the run, with the slice decision and power check committed separately at 80533fe -- also before the run. That second commitment is STRICTER than the script: 'deep-tail MCB is the least-powered part of this experiment on the production slice. If MCB comes back inconclusive -- CI containing zero rather than clearly favourable -- that is NOT a pass by default; it triggers the wide-slice re-run before anything is adopted.'
experiments.result: The SCRIPT's six conditions all pass and it printed ADOPT. Treated vs control, 5 folds, 1,681 episodes matched exactly across all three arms, Bonferroni 98.75%: pooled -0.03263 CI [-0.04356, -0.01402], 5 of 5 folds; spike -0.33274 CI [-0.58775, -0.09013], 5 of 5; calm -0.01744 (-8.22%) CI [-0.02955, -0.00766], 4 of 5; coverage error -0.00083 (an improvement) CI [-0.00411, +0.00300]; placebo margin -0.03493 CI [-0.04451, -0.01558]. The placebo behaves as a placebo must: pooled +0.00230 (hurts), calm +0.00596 with a CI EXCLUDING zero (hurts), and it captures only about a quarter of the spike gain (-0.08525 against the treated arm's -0.33274). BUT DEEP-TAIL MCB IS INCONCLUSIVE: +0.00056, CI [-0.00010, +0.00255], 3 of 5 folds WORSE. The interval contains zero, so the script's guard passes; the point estimate is on the unfavourable side and it is not clearly favourable.
experiments.implication: ADOPTION IS WITHHELD, by the stricter commitment I recorded before the run rather than by the script. This is exactly the case that commitment named, and E-power is why it was named: MCB is the quantity that gains MOST from a wider slice (2.98x, the largest of the four E-power measured), so an inconclusive MCB on the production slice is the predicted failure mode, not a surprise. The wide-slice re-run is launched. SEPARATELY, a strong consistency result: E2c measured pooled -0.03264 on a re-weighted median; the FULL PIPELINE gives -0.03263. The barrier curves, the committee and the calibration neither amplified nor destroyed the effect. And the control arms reproduced E-anchor's fold values to four decimals across three separate runs, confirming post_shift_fn=None is genuinely inert.
experiments.lesson: A script that implements a rule is not the same as the rule. The pre-registration had two parts -- the guards inside iv_confirm.py and the stricter slice commitment in the ledger -- and only the first was executable. When they disagreed the executable one said ADOPT. Honouring the stricter one is the whole point of writing it down before seeing the number.

experiments.question: Are the funding-rate features buildable, causal, and adequately covered?
experiments.rule: Same protocol as ivfeatures: strict a >= h+1 causality, a dense hourly grid so a missing hour becomes NaN rather than reading a neighbour, per-feature coverage through noctua.splits.time_splits, a leakage check with a positive-control decoy that MUST be caught, units established from the data rather than asserted, and anything unbuildable marked BLOCKED with no substitute. Every headline number re-derived by me before it counts.
experiments.result: Built as model/eval/fundingfeatures.py with 7 features; none BLOCKED. RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY AND ALL CONFIRMED: 64,206 rows, strictly increasing, 0 duplicates, 64,204 hourly gaps and exactly one 10,800s gap at 2020-08-27 05:00 UTC, span 2019-04-30 10:00 -> 2026-08-26 17:00. Positional alignment with episodes.parquet verified True. Coverage: fund_rate 67.8/100/100 train/calib/test, matching my own causal-join computation exactly; trailing-window features lower in TRAIN only (fund_z_20d 65.7%, fund_cum_7d 67.1%) from burn-in plus the no-stale-fill rule, and unaffected in calib/test. UNITS, re-derived: interest_8h tracks the trailing 8-hour SUM of interest_1h at corr 0.9990 and median relative error 0.37%, against 87.49% for the trailing MEAN and 87.88% for interest_1h * 8. So interest_1h is the additive per-hour building block, and the cumulative features correctly sum it -- summing interest_8h would have overcounted each hour ~8x through overlapping windows.
experiments.implication: THE MOST VALUABLE THING THE BUILD PRODUCED WAS A FAILURE, NOT A FEATURE. The positive-control decoy initially caught only 9 of 10 boundary trials. Cause, verified by me: ivfeatures.py corrupts with a PURE MULTIPLIER, v -> v*uniform(2,5), which is sound for DVOL (minimum 19.17, never zero) and SILENTLY BLIND for the funding rate, where 11,435 of 64,206 values -- 17.8%, and the 25th percentile itself -- are exactly 0.0. 0 * anything == 0, so those rows were never tested and would have reported a clean pass. An affine corruption v*factor + offset restored 10/10. Recorded as pitfalls check 12, check_corruption_bites: a corruption used in a leakage test must be verified to have MOVED every row it claims to have corrupted. A style that is safe for one series is not thereby safe for another.
experiments.lesson: Copying an audited reference implementation transfers its assumptions along with its discipline. ivfeatures.py was audited and correct FOR DVOL; the property that made it correct -- a strictly positive series -- was never stated, so it did not travel with the code.

experiments.question: Does E2c's IV correction survive the full pipeline on the wide slice, where the deep-tail MCB guard has power?
experiments.rule: The ORIGINAL rule, unchanged after seeing the production result: pooled QLIKE CI clears zero favourably at Bonferroni 98.75%; deep-tail MCB not worse; spike not worse; calm within 1% of the calm base; beats the placebo; conditional coverage error not worse. Triggered by the pre-commitment at 80533fe that an inconclusive production MCB is not a pass by default.
experiments.result: PASSES ALL SIX CONDITIONS on the 24-anchor-hour slice. 40,351 episodes matched exactly across all three arms, 5 folds. pooled -0.01734 CI [-0.02986, -0.00967], 5 of 5 folds; spike -0.08388 CI [-0.17731, -0.03128], 5 of 5; calm -0.01408 (-5.46%) CI [-0.02376, -0.00715], 4 of 5; DEEP-TAIL MCB -0.00069 CI [-0.00183, +0.00183], 3 of 5 BETTER -- the point estimate FLIPPED to the favourable side from +0.00056 on production; coverage error +0.00038 CI [-0.00160, +0.00199], not worse; placebo margin -0.01919 CI [-0.03359, -0.00883].
experiments.implication: THE EFFECT IS ROUGHLY HALF THE SIZE ON THE WIDE SLICE and this must not be buried: pooled -11.61% on production against -6.18% on all hours; spike -0.33274 against -0.08388, a factor of four. Both remain 5 of 5 folds with CIs excluding zero, so the effect is real on both slices, but THE PRODUCTION-SLICE ESTIMATE OF THE BENEFIT IS OPTIMISTIC. The same two readings E-power left open apply and this data does not separate them: either the 17:00 anchor genuinely carries a larger effect, or the production estimate is inflated by the smaller sample. For planning purposes the WIDE-SLICE number is the conservative one and should be quoted. STATUS IS CONFIRMED CANDIDATE, NOT PRODUCTION-READY. The shipped model is unchanged. Remaining gates before any GO: independent audit of implementation, statistics, timestamps/leakage and result reduction; a genuinely untouched holdout, which does not yet exist; multiple-testing correction across the whole experiment family, not just the IV family; and an honest economic assessment.
experiments.lesson: The pre-commitment did its job in both directions. It withheld adoption when the production MCB was inconclusive, and the wide-slice run it forced returned an MCB that was not merely inconclusive but favourably signed -- while also revealing the headline effect is half what production suggested. Had adoption gone ahead on the production result, the shipped claim would have been roughly twice the truth.

experiments.question: Does any historical period remain genuinely untouched and usable as a final holdout?
experiments.rule: A period that influenced training, calibration, feature selection, model selection, hyperparameters, experiment design, debugging, threshold choice or a go/no-go decision is NOT an untouched holdout. Renaming previously examined data does not create one. The untouched holdout gets exactly ONE evaluation.
experiments.result: NO. Verified per year against noctua.splits and the walk-forward folds, recorded in model/research/DATA_USE.md. 2017-2022 trained on (2017 partial from SAMPLE_START = 2017-08-01). 2023 and part of 2024 calibrated on. 2024-2026 scored as test. 2021-2026 have EVERY year serving as a walk-forward test fold in at least six experiments on overlapping data: E-anchor-verdict, E-blend, E-blend-1state, E2-iv-correction, E2b-result, E2c-result, E-power-result, E2-confirm-result, E2-confirm-wide. 2012-2016 sits before SAMPLE_START and was never trained on, but is ALSO disqualified: it influenced experiment design through the coverage computations that produced the residual-correction design, and SAMPLE_START is itself a modelling choice, so scoring there would be a distribution-shift test rather than a holdout.
experiments.implication: FORWARD PAPER-TRADING HOLDOUT, frozen 2026-08-28 UTC. Holdout is observations with anchor timestamp strictly after the freeze. The ~19 days between the last episode in episodes.parquet (2026-08-09) and the freeze are NOT holdout -- they were available to be examined and are disqualified by the same standard. The frozen candidate is E2c: five features (iv_chg_1h, iv_chg_6h, iv_chg_24h, iv_z_20d, ivrv_ratio), no intercept, SIGMA_B = 0.10, coefficients fitted on pre-freeze data only. No refits, no feature changes, no re-tuning against holdout performance. POWER, stated before the fact: E-power showed the binding constraint is independent year-scale regimes, not episodes. At roughly one regime-observation per year, a forward holdout resolving a 6.18% pooled effect on FOLD-LEVEL inference needs years, not weeks. A per-episode paired test is far better powered and is the right primary, but it measures sampling error rather than the between-regime variation that dominates. Both get reported and the fold-level one is labelled underpowered until it is not.
experiments.lesson: The honest answer to 'do we have a holdout' was no, and it was worth asking explicitly rather than assuming the test split still counted. The test split has been scored in nine experiments and has shaped feature selection; it stopped being a holdout long before anyone asked.

experiments.question: Are the four horizons and the two distinct label families buildable, and what are the correct baselines?
experiments.rule: Inspection before building, per the protocol. Establish from the code and the data what targets exist, whether 'closes higher' and 'barrier touched' are genuinely separate labels, and what base rate a direction model actually has to beat. No hypothesis is tested here.
experiments.result: HORIZONS: episodes.build_episodes already takes a --horizons argument, DEFAULT_HORIZONS = (6, 12, 19, 24). The requested 1h and 1w (168h) are not built but are buildable through the SAME code path, which satisfies RULES R18. Current counts: H=6 127,080; H=12 127,666; H=19 127,853; H=24 127,897, over all 24 anchor hours. LABELS ARE ALREADY SEPARATE, verified from source: R = log(s_T) - log(s_tau), the TERMINAL log return, where s_tau is the previous hour's close and s_T is the close of hour a+H-1. M_up / M_dn are the running EXCURSION extrema. The pathwise identities M_up >= max(0,R) and M_dn <= min(0,R) hold with zero violations. THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE AND THE GAP IS LARGE: at a 2% barrier, P(touch) vs P(close beyond) is 0.1720/0.0890 at H=6, 0.2790/0.1462 at H=12, 0.3652/0.1955 at H=19, 0.4106/0.2229 at H=24 -- a ratio near 1.9x at every horizon.
experiments.implication: THE DIRECTION BASE RATE IS NOT 0.5. P(R>0) is 0.5177 at H=6, 0.5237 at H=12, 0.5281 at H=19 and 0.5328 at H=24, rising with horizon as BTC's upward drift accumulates. Any direction model must beat THAT number, not 0.5 -- an 'accuracy 53%' claim at H=24 is exactly the base rate and is worth nothing. This also means a constant-probability forecast at the rolling base rate is a genuine baseline with real skill against a 0.5 reference, and it must be in the comparison set. For volatility, mean RV rises 0.01922 -> 0.02794 -> 0.03579 -> 0.04056 across the four horizons, so QLIKE is not comparable across horizons and each needs its own baseline table.
experiments.lesson: The 'do not mix closes-higher with barrier-touched' instruction was already satisfied structurally in the episode builder, but nobody had quantified how different the two events are. At a 1.9x ratio, a model evaluated on the wrong one would look catastrophically miscalibrated for a reason that has nothing to do with its skill.

experiments.question: Are the four protocol horizons (1h/6h/1d/1w) buildable, and what do their targets look like?
experiments.rule: Build through the SAME code path (RULES R18) and PROVE it by reproducing the overlapping horizons from the frozen artifact exactly (R19). Write to a separate file -- episodes.parquet is frozen and everything depends on it.
experiments.result: Built model/artifacts/episodes_h4.parquet: 506,613 episodes at H = 1, 6, 24, 168 from the existing 128,031-row hourly table, in 1 second. REPRODUCTION PROOF: H=6 and H=24 match the frozen episodes.parquet with max |diff| = 0.000e+00 across R, M_up, M_dn, RV and s_tau, at identical row counts (127,080 and 127,897). The new H=1 and H=168 therefore came from the same code path. Counts: H=1 123,773; H=6 127,080; H=24 127,897; H=168 127,863.
experiments.implication: BASE RATES RISE MONOTONICALLY WITH HORIZON: P(R>0) = 0.5089 / 0.5177 / 0.5328 / 0.5506 at 1h / 6h / 1d / 1w. At one week the base rate is 55.06%, so a direction model there must clear 55% before it has demonstrated anything at all. TOUCH AND CLOSE DIVERGE AT EVERY HORIZON, ratio 1.89 / 1.93 / 1.84 / 1.78 at a 2% barrier. At 1w, P(touch 2%) = 0.7571 against P(close beyond 2%) = 0.4243. MEAN RV SPANS 16x, 0.00726 at 1h to 0.11469 at 1w, so QLIKE is not comparable across horizons and each needs its own baseline table. EMBARGO: time_splits derives embargo_hours from max(H), so including H=168 raises it to 168h automatically -- horizon-appropriate rather than fixed. Cost is modest: train 189,110 / calib 51,644 / test 73,726.
experiments.lesson: THE 1w HORIZON IS FAR LESS INFORMATIVE THAN ITS ROW COUNT SUGGESTS. Consecutive hourly anchors share 167 of their 168 hours, so effective independent weekly episodes are about 52 per year, not 8,760. Any 1w experiment must state its MDE against ~52 independent observations per year, not the nominal count -- this is E-power's finding in a sharper form, and it applies before any 1w experiment is designed.

experiments.question: Before building any direction model: which horizons can a 6-fold experiment actually resolve?
experiments.rule: RULES R5 applied before the fact. Measure the fold-level noise floor from a comparison that contains NO model -- two baselines differing only in how they estimate the base rate -- and compare the resulting MDE against the effect size prior work measured (direction skill 0.180%, i.e. BSS 0.0018, against 4.98% on barriers). Any horizon whose MDE exceeds that is a NON-MEASUREMENT before it runs and must be redesigned or not run.
experiments.result: THREE OF FOUR HORIZONS ARE NOT POWERED AT THE FOLD LEVEL. MDE at 80% power, expressed as a Brier Skill Score, from 6 walk-forward folds: H=1 0.0008 (POWERED, below the 0.0018 prior effect); H=6 0.0042 (NOT POWERED, 2.3x too coarse); H=24 0.0168 (NOT POWERED, 9.3x); H=168 0.0517 (NOT POWERED, 29x). Underlying fold-level sd of the Brier difference: 0.000167 / 0.000913 / 0.003651 / 0.011194. SEPARATE NULL WORTH HAVING: the mean difference is POSITIVE at every horizon (+0.000053 / +0.000320 / +0.001855 / +0.006469), meaning the RECENT base rate scores WORSE than the long-run one. Base-rate drift is real -- P(R>0) ranges 0.4467 to 0.6360 across years at H=168 -- but it is not exploitable by simply tracking it.
experiments.implication: REDESIGN, not abandonment. E-power already established the remedy: the fold-level bootstrap measures between-year heterogeneity, and a PAIRED PER-EPISODE block bootstrap measures sampling error at n in the 100,000s. For direction the paired estimator becomes PRIMARY and the fold-level one becomes a stability check that is reported and labelled underpowered rather than treated as the verdict. AN UNCOMFORTABLE TENSION, named now rather than discovered later: H=1 is the only fold-level-powered horizon AND the least economically useful one -- highest turnover, most cost-sensitive, smallest per-trade edge. A direction result that is only statistically resolvable where it is least tradable is a warning about the whole enterprise, not a finding to celebrate.
experiments.lesson: STRUCTURAL FACT FOUND WHILE MEASURING THIS: walk_forward_folds leaves a 186-DAY GAP between the end of TRAIN and the start of TEST. The calib slice bridges it, ending 2 days before test. So any 'recent history' quantity must be estimated from CALIB, not TRAIN -- my first attempt used the train mask and produced an exactly-zero difference at every horizon, because the recent window was empty and silently fell back to the unconditional estimate. A comparison that returns exactly 0.000000 six times is a bug signature, not a null.

experiments.question: Does any direction model beat the rolling base rate as a PROBABILITY forecast, at any horizon?
experiments.rule: Pre-registered and committed BEFORE the harness is run. POPULATION: episodes_h4.parquet, walk-forward folds, test slices only. All arms scored on identical episodes. Probabilities calibrated on the CALIB slice only, never on test. PRIMARY: Brier Skill Score against the CALIB-WINDOW base rate baseline, with a PAIRED PER-EPISODE moving-block bootstrap CI that must exclude zero favourably. Paired is primary because direction-power showed the fold-level estimator is NOT POWERED at H=6, 24 and 168 -- MDE 0.0042 / 0.0168 / 0.0517 BSS against a 0.0018 prior effect. The fold-level interval is reported as a stability check and LABELLED UNDERPOWERED at those three horizons; only H=1 (MDE 0.0008) is fold-level powered. BASELINE LADDER, all required, in increasing order of sophistication: (a) unconditional base rate from train; (b) calib-window base rate -- THE BASELINE TO BEAT; (c) logistic regression on the existing causal feature set; (d) gradient boosting. Anything that does not beat (b) has demonstrated nothing, since P(R>0) is 0.5089-0.5506 and rises with horizon, so beating 0.5 is not evidence. GUARDS, all must hold: calibration slope in [0.8, 1.2] and intercept within 0.02 of zero on the test slice; AUC reported but NOT a pass condition; must beat a row-shuffled label control; must beat a circular-time-shift placebo of the feature block. MULTIPLE TESTING: this is a NEW family (direction), separate from the IV family, and every arm counts including failures. Bonferroni within the family at minimum; the family size is fixed now at 4 model classes x 4 horizons = 16. REJECTION: if the paired CI contains zero against baseline (b), direction is not predictable by that model class at that horizon and the result is recorded as such.
experiments.result:
NULL AT EVERY HORIZON. 16 of 16 arms fail the pre-registered rule; not one model arm beats the calib-window base rate as a probability forecast, and every model arm is WORSE. Brier / BSS-vs-calib / AUC / calibration slope, pooled over 6 folds:
  H=1   (n=49,118) logistic 0.25107 -0.00398 auc 0.5091 slope 0.031 | gbm 0.25097 -0.00361 auc 0.5123 slope 0.022
  H=6   (n=49,124) logistic 0.25286 -0.00972 auc 0.5046 slope 0.012 | gbm 0.25119 -0.00306 auc 0.5128 slope 0.038
  H=24  (n=49,106) logistic 0.25887 -0.02652 auc 0.4961 slope -0.007 | gbm 0.25692 -0.01877 auc 0.5029 slope -0.017
  H=168 (n=48,962) logistic 0.26302 -0.02128 auc 0.5036 slope 0.008 | gbm 0.27675 -0.07458 auc 0.5117 slope -0.036
The paired per-episode CI -- the pre-registered primary -- excludes zero on the WRONG side (arm worse than baseline) in 6 of the 8 model rows, and straddles zero in the other two. No arm clears. NEGATIVE CONTROLS BEHAVED: the row-shuffled-label control is negative at all four horizons (-0.00467 / -0.00678 / -0.00862 / -0.00486), so the harness is not manufacturing skill; the circular-time-shift placebo is also negative everywhere. The CALIBRATION GUARD is the sharpest reading of the result: slopes are 0.001 to 0.038 in absolute value against a required [0.8, 1.2]. A slope near zero means the SPREAD in the predicted probabilities carries no information about the outcome -- the models are confidently varying their forecasts and the variation is noise. The H=1 reliability table shows it directly: the top decile predicts 0.580 and realizes 0.528, the bottom predicts 0.446 and realizes 0.495, and the middle is not monotone.
experiments.implication:
DIRECTION IS CLOSED AS A PROBABILITY-FORECASTING PROBLEM at these four horizons with this feature set and these two model classes, and the failure is not a power failure -- the paired estimator has n ~ 49,000 and its intervals are narrow enough to EXCLUDE zero in the adverse direction. This is a measured absence, not an unresolved question.
THREE OBSERVATIONS THAT SURVIVE THE NULL, none of which changes the verdict:
(1) AUC sits at 0.5029-0.5128 for gbm at all four horizons -- always above 0.5, never by more than 1.3 percentage points. If there is rank information it is at that scale, and it is more than destroyed by the probability miscalibration. AUC was pre-registered as NOT a pass condition precisely so this could not be promoted into a result after the fact.
(2) At H=168 the TRAIN base rate beats the CALIB base rate with a paired CI that excludes zero ([-0.013279, -0.000996], BSS +0.02749). That is a finding about BASE-RATE INSTABILITY, not about direction: the calibration window (2023-01 to 2024-07) had an unrepresentative drift, so the most recent estimate was the worse estimate. It vindicates the choice to pre-register the calib-window base rate as the bar -- against the train base rate the models would have looked even worse.
(3) The negative controls are not decoration. The placebo at H=1 posts BSS -0.01864, four to five times worse than the real models, which is what a working placebo looks like.
experiments.lesson: The calibration slope did more work here than the Brier score. A model with no signal does not produce a flat forecast -- it produces a CONFIDENT, VARYING forecast whose variation is noise, and the Brier score penalises that only mildly (0.2510 against 0.2501) while the calibration slope reports it as 0.03 against a required 1.0. Pre-registering calibration as a PASS condition and AUC as a REPORTED-ONLY one is what kept this from being written up as 'AUC 0.512, a small but consistent edge'.

experiments.question: Does the IV result survive independent adversarial statistical and data audit?
experiments.rule: Two independent auditors briefed to DISPROVE, not defend. Every finding re-derived by me before acting on it, per the standing rule that no agent result enters the record unverified.
experiments.result:
THE RESULT DOES NOT STAND AS STATED. Four severe findings, all independently confirmed by me:
(1) THE PRIMARY STATISTIC COULD NOT FAIL. With n=5 fold deltas all sharing a sign, every bootstrap resample is a convex combination of negatives, so the interval is negative AT EVERY ALPHA by construction. Verified: the CI is [-0.02986, -0.00967] at alpha=0.05/4, and IDENTICAL at 0.05/40 and 0.05/1000. This is RULES R2 -- a rule that cannot fail is not a rule -- applied to my own primary endpoint, and I did not catch it despite having written that rule.
(2) HONEST ESTIMATORS DO NOT CLEAR. t-interval unadjusted [-0.03449, -0.00019] barely excludes zero (p=0.0485); at family=4 it is [-0.04399, +0.00932] and CONTAINS ZERO; at family=9, [-0.05092, +0.01625]. The exact sign-flip permutation test gives one-sided p = 0.03125, which is THE MINIMUM ATTAINABLE at n=5 -- it cannot clear any Bonferroni threshold with family >= 2, however strong the true effect.
(3) BOTH EFFECTS ARE BELOW THEIR OWN MDE, computed with the correct noncentral-t rather than the z approximation I used: production observed 11.61% against MDE 11.81%; wide observed 6.18% against MDE 8.19%. By this project's own R5, both are NON-MEASUREMENTS.
(4) THE PAIRED PER-EPISODE ESTIMATOR DOES NOT EXIST. `paired_per_episode` is None in BOTH anchor_freshness.json and anchor_freshness_allhours.json. BENCHMARK 26 and its commit message state the estimator 'now records' the paired comparison. THAT CLAIM IS FALSE and is withdrawn.
experiments.implication: STATUS DOWNGRADED from CONFIRMED CANDIDATE to NOT PROVEN. The shipped model was never changed and is not changed now. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is not nothing: the effect is directionally consistent (5 of 5 folds on both slices), beats a coverage-preserving placebo, reverses completely under a test-shuffle positive control, is 89.5% episode-varying rather than a disguised intercept, and is insensitive to the shrinkage constant across eight orders of magnitude. That is a real, mechanistically plausible signal. It is NOT a statistically established one at any defensible corrected level. SEPARATELY, the data auditor raised an UNRESOLVED threat: Deribit's volatility- index endpoint returns CANDLES, and if the timestamp marks candle OPEN rather than CLOSE -- the prevailing exchange convention -- then reading the close stamped at h from anchor h+1 cancels the entire safety margin. The endpoint is unreachable from this container and the docs do not state the convention. No leakage test here can catch it, because they all check the code against the ts column rather than against real publication timing.
experiments.lesson: I wrote R2 -- 'a rule that cannot fail is not a rule' -- after finding five such guards, and then used a primary endpoint that could not fail. The bootstrap saturation was even NOTICED and reported in BENCHMARK 25 as 'an artifact of n, not significance', and I still let it stand as the primary rather than replacing the estimator. Noticing a defect and continuing to rely on it is worse than missing it.

experiments.question: Does the IV effect survive an estimator that is actually capable of failing?
experiments.rule: The audit's finding 1 was that the fold-level bootstrap could not return a null with 5 same-signed folds. The replacement estimator must therefore be shown to PASS THE R2 TEST itself -- demonstrated capable of failing -- before its result is quoted. Computed from the cached components, no retraining.
experiments.result:
PAIRED PER-EPISODE, n = 1,681 episodes over 5 folds. Mean paired delta -0.031000, sd 0.33977. Block bootstrap excludes zero at EVERY family size tested: unadjusted [-0.047516, -0.016216]; family=4 [-0.052996, -0.012516]; family=9 [-0.056025, -0.010772]; family=47 [-0.059800, -0.007053]. Observed |0.031000| is ABOVE its MDE of 0.023204.
R2 TEST ON THE NEW STATISTIC -- PASSES. Episode deltas take both signs, 902 better and 779 worse (53.7% / 46.3%), so a resample CAN come out positive. Demonstrated: a random 120-episode subsample of the SAME data gives mean -0.00508, CI [-0.03831, +0.02610], which does NOT exclude zero. A smaller sample failing is what a functioning test looks like, and is precisely what the fold-level statistic could never do.
experiments.implication:
This is the estimator E-power identified as the remedy and BENCHMARK 26 wrongly claimed already existed. It answers a DIFFERENT question from the fold-level one, and both belong in the record: the paired estimator measures whether the correction helps EPISODE BY EPISODE, and it does, robustly to a 47-member family. The fold-level estimator asks whether the effect is stable ACROSS YEARS, and at n=5 it cannot answer that at any corrected level -- the exact sign-flip permutation floor of 1/32 forbids it.
So the honest statement is narrower than 28's and wider than 29's: the effect is established at the episode level and UNRESOLVED at the year level. Since E-power showed between-year heterogeneity dominates, the year-level question is the one that matters for deployment, and it remains open.
EFFECTIVE-N CAUTION, stated rather than buried: production episodes are one per day at H=19, so adjacent episodes share 18 of their 19 hours. The block bootstrap uses blocks of 12 episodes, about 12 days, which models that overlap; the naive t-test (p = 1.9e-4) does not and is not relied on.
experiments.lesson: The audit's finding that the paired estimator 'does not exist' was correct about the ARTIFACTS and wrong about the cause. The code path is sound -- it simply never ran, because anchor_freshness.json was produced by --from-json (which stores no per-episode arrays) and the all-hours run had already imported the module before the patch landed. The false claim in 26 stands withdrawn either way: 'the code records this' and 'the artifact contains this' are different statements and I conflated them.

experiments.question: Does the IV effect depend on Deribit's candle-timestamp convention -- the audit's highest-threat finding?
experiments.rule: Rather than resolve an unresolvable question, make the result immune to it. A 2-hour lag is correct under EITHER convention: if the stamp marks candle CLOSE the original 1-hour lag was already safe, and if it marks candle OPEN then 2 hours restores the full margin. Scored with the PAIRED estimator, which was separately demonstrated capable of failing.
experiments.result: THE THREAT IS NEUTRALISED. The effect does not weaken under the extra hour -- it is marginally STRONGER. 1h lag: mean -0.031000, CI(family=9) [-0.056025, -0.010772], 5 of 5 folds better. 2h lag: mean -0.033551, CI(family=9) [-0.060379, -0.010460], 4 of 5 folds better. Retention 108.2%. Both clear the corrected interval. The 2-hour build passes its own leakage suite independently: all six features CAUSAL, max_violation 0.000e+00, and the positive-control decoy caught in 10/10 trials.
experiments.implication: The audit's finding 1 -- that a candle-OPEN timestamp convention would cancel the entire safety margin and no test here could detect it -- no longer threatens the result. Under either convention the correction works, so the convention need not be established. This is the right shape of answer to an unresolvable data question: engineer around it rather than argue it. The mildly lower fold consistency at 2h (4 of 5 rather than 5 of 5) is reported rather than smoothed over; the mean effect is larger and the interval still clears, so the two move in opposite directions and neither is decisive on its own.
experiments.lesson: An unresolvable question can sometimes be made irrelevant. The endpoint is unreachable from this container and the docs do not state the convention, so the question could not be settled -- but it could be rendered moot by a design that is correct under every possible answer, at a cost of one hour of feature freshness.

experiments.question: Are the audit's mechanical findings fixed, and can the defects recur?
experiments.rule: Every audit finding either fixed with a test that proves the fix, or explicitly declined with a reason. A guard written in prose must have a test showing it can fail.
experiments.result:
THREE FIXES, each verified.
(1) pitfalls check 13, check_bootstrap_can_fail: refuses a resampling interval whose observations all share a sign, since every resample is then a convex combination of them and the interval excludes zero at every alpha. Its historical case is E2-confirm's own five wide-slice fold deltas. It also returns the exact sign-flip floor 2^-n, so a design that cannot reach corrected significance is detectable BEFORE it runs. Self-test now expects 13 failures and passes.
(2) direction.small_n_inference: the t-interval, the exact sign-flip permutation test, and an MDE built from noncentral-t rather than the z approximation (z_.975 + z_.80 = 2.80) that understated it by 25-35% at n = 5-6. Verified on E2-confirm's own deltas: t-CI unadjusted [-0.03449, -0.00019] clears; family=4 [-0.04399, +0.00932] does NOT; permutation p = 0.03125, exactly AT the 2^-5 floor.
(3) The placebo rotation is now derived from the data instead of asserted. Verified: the covered set is 186,663 rows over 1,944.8 days = 95.98 rows/day, so the old 8,760-row constant moved 91.3 days while both the code and BENCHMARK 24 claimed 365. The new computation gives 35,034 rows = 365.0 days, matching its own claim.
experiments.implication: The bootstrap defect is now impossible to repeat silently: any experiment that runs check 13 on same-signed fold deltas gets a FAIL with the reason and the permutation floor attached. That closes the specific way this project's most promising result was over-stated. ONE AUDIT RECOMMENDATION IS DECLINED WITH A REASON RATHER THAN SILENTLY SKIPPED: Romano-Wolf stepdown across the full ~47-experiment family. It needs a shared resampling scheme over the raw per-fold statistic of EVERY family member, and the ledger stores only summary deltas and intervals for almost all of them. It cannot be retrofitted without re-running the family, which is real missing infrastructure and is recorded as such rather than pretended away.
experiments.lesson: The placebo bug is the clearest example yet of RULES R17: a constant named PLACEBO_SHIFT_H, carrying an _H suffix for hours, used as a row index. The name asserted a unit the code did not honour, and the docstring repeated the assertion, and BENCHMARK 24 repeated it again. Three statements of the same unchecked claim.

experiments.question: Does the 'beats the placebo' guard survive the corrected 365-day rotation?
experiments.rule: The placebo changed, so the guard is re-run rather than assumed to carry. Scored with the paired estimator at family=9, the same instrument used everywhere else after the audit.
experiments.result: THE GUARD SURVIVES, with a smaller margin. real features    mean -0.031000, CI(fam=9) [-0.055204, -0.010411], 5 of 5 folds. placebo OLD 91-day    mean +0.002229, CI contains zero, 2 of 5 folds. placebo CORRECTED 365-day  mean -0.007767, CI [-0.020899, +0.002936] contains zero, 3 of 5 folds. MARGIN vs the corrected placebo: -0.023232, CI(fam=9) [-0.044132, -0.003974], CLEARS. Against the old 91-day placebo the margin was -0.033229.
experiments.implication: The corrected placebo is a HARDER test and the effect still beats it, so the conclusion is unchanged -- but the margin shrinks by 30%, from -0.0332 to -0.0232, and that is reported rather than buried. WHY THE YEAR-ROTATED PLACEBO SCORES BETTER THAN THE 91-DAY ONE, stated as a hypothesis and not a finding: a 365-day rotation lands on the SAME CALENDAR POSITION one year earlier, so if implied vol carries annual seasonality the rotated series retains genuine information. That would make the 365-day placebo not purely uninformative -- which is CONSERVATIVE for this guard, since it raises the bar, but it means the placebo margin is a lower bound on the true signal-versus-noise gap rather than an unbiased estimate of it.
experiments.lesson: A fix to a control is not neutral -- it changes the test. Correcting the rotation from 91 to 365 days moved the placebo's own score from +0.0022 to -0.0078 and cut the margin 30%. Had the correction gone the other way, the guard could have failed, and 'we fixed a bug' would have been the reason a result disappeared.

experiments.question: What is the locked statistical protocol, after the audit?
experiments.rule: Locked AFTER the adversarial audit, not before -- locking it earlier and revising it afterwards would have violated R1. Every rule in it is enforceable by a check in research/pitfalls.py; a rule with no executable check is a preference, not a protocol.
experiments.result: model/research/STATS_PROTOCOL.md. Seven sections: which estimator is primary (paired per-episode wherever pairing exists; fold-level is a stability check, never primary unless shown powered in advance); what is forbidden at small n (a bootstrap over same-signed observations, and quoting a confidence level the estimator cannot respond to); what replaces it (t-interval, exact sign-flip permutation, noncentral-t MDE, all three reported together because they disagree usefully); MDE stated before every experiment with the known values tabulated; multiple testing over the honest family; controls; and what a guard must satisfy. THE PERMUTATION FLOOR IS NOW A PRE-RUN CHECK: one-sided p cannot go below 2^-n, so a design whose floor exceeds its corrected threshold CANNOT SUCCEED and is redesigned or declared underpowered before compute is spent. RULES.md gains R29-R33, all earned this session: a fix to a control changes the test; a resampling interval over same-signed observations is not a test; noticing a defect and continuing to rely on it is worse than missing it; an unresolvable question can be made irrelevant; 'the code does X' and 'the artifact contains X' are different claims.
experiments.implication: Romano-Wolf is named as the right tool and recorded as UNAVAILABLE with the reason -- it needs raw per-fold statistics for every family member and the ledger stores only summaries, so retrofitting means re-running the family. Bonferroni over the honest family size is the conservative fallback until that infrastructure exists. Recorded as missing rather than waved away.

experiments.question: Does NOCTUA's own headline claim -- that it beats Log-HAR -- survive the protocol just locked?
experiments.rule: Apply the locked protocol to the INCUMBENT, not only to candidates. A standard applied only to challengers is not a standard. Computed from the cached out-of-sample components, no retraining.
experiments.result:
THE SAME EPISTEMIC POSITION AS THE NEW CANDIDATE, which is the point of checking. Per-fold deltas -0.02216 / -0.01049 / +0.01563 / -0.02031 / -0.02317 / -0.03091, so 5 of 6 folds better and 2023 the exception. Relative improvement -4.98%.
FOLD LEVEL (n=6): deltas are NOT all same-signed, so a bootstrap here IS a legitimate test -- unlike E2c's, and that distinction matters. But the t-interval unadjusted is [-0.03253, +0.00206] and DOES NOT CLEAR; permutation one-sided p = 0.04688 against a floor of 0.01562; and observed |0.01524| is BELOW the noncentral-t MDE of 0.02348.
PAIRED PER-EPISODE (n=2,046): 1,157 episodes better and 889 worse, so the estimator can fail. Mean -0.014127, clearing at unadjusted [-0.020651, -0.006773], at family=9 [-0.023396, -0.003810], and at family=47 [-0.024995, -0.002314].
experiments.implication: The project's headline claim was NEVER fold-level significant either. It is established episode by episode and unresolved across years, exactly like E2c. That is the fair comparison and it changes how both should be described: the new candidate is not held to a bar the incumbent clears, because the incumbent does not clear it. This also puts the 4.98% figure in context. BENCHMARK's model table reports NOCTUA 0.290346 against log_har 0.305651 as a settled ranking. It is settled at the episode level; at the year level, with six folds, it is below the minimum detectable effect and one fold (2023) reverses it.
experiments.lesson: A standard applied only to challengers is not a standard, it is a moat. Running the protocol against the incumbent was the obvious next step and I nearly went off to build new benchmarks instead.

experiments.question: Before building the four-horizon volatility matrix: which rows can a 6-fold experiment resolve?
experiments.rule: STATS_PROTOCOL section 4 applied before the build. Noise floor from a model-free comparison -- persistence against a per-fold OLS Log-HAR fit -- so the MDE is a property of the design, not of any candidate. Reference effect size is NOCTUA's own measured advantage over Log-HAR, 4.98% (incumbent-under-protocol).
